findings.where: Step 3 (The small cell runs out) text, step 4 Why, explain paragraph 2, and step 5's 'Ampere-hours through string' readout
findings.what: Step 3 says the string 'cannot reach' the 100 Ah left in the big tanks, but two screens later the strong cells push 10 A on through the empty cell, drain to 0 Ah and the readout climbs to 100 Ah, so say instead that the string can only reach that charge by driving the empty cell backwards, so its useful capacity, where its volts drop away, is 80 Ah, and stop or label the readout past 8 h so the forced 20 Ah does not look like capacity.

findings.where: SHOW steps 3, 5, 9 and 11 (text, the 'to try it' line and the live line under the control)
findings.what: Counted the way Dan reads the screen, these carry about 104, 109, 110 and 107 words (steps 1 and 7 about 93 and 98), over the 90-word cap, and the live lines repeat the screen's own last sentence (step 9's '2.20 V each', step 3's 'still hold 20 Ah'), so cut each screen to about 90 in all, starting with step 5's two 'In a long string' sentences, which the explain already carries.

The lesson carries nine [^n] marks, far more than 'a few a lesson', and [^4], [^5], [^7] and [^8] sit on plain statements he would never look up (the cell is empty at 8 hours, its voltage turns round, heat and gas, starved of charge), so keep only the float voltage, the band and the parallel-string rule.

findings.where: Step 7 (Full first) text and explain paragraph 4
findings.what: The screen sets up 'charges from flat' but never says why that matters: after an ordinary part-discharge from full, every cell needs the same ampere-hours back and they fill together, so one sentence saying the weak cell gets ahead only from flat, or on float, would stop him wondering whether this happens on every recharge.

It says the odd cell 'sits in overcharge at 2.38 V' with no reason on the screen, while the explain gives one (its plates take no more charge, so its voltage climbs), so swap 'slightly starved' for that clause to keep the step whole within the word cap.

findings.where: Step 11 (Strings in parallel) text and explain paragraph 7
findings.what: 'Both see the same volts, so the current splits inversely' skips why two sources split like resistors: with equal emfs on the same bars, each path loses the same volts, so each current is those volts divided by its path resistance; say that in one sentence.
'The weak cell limits how long the string runs, not how hard' is absolute, but a faded cell usually has a higher internal resistance too, which is why impedance is trended, so say 'mainly how long'.
'So the smallest length sets what the whole circuit can carry' reads as the shortest length, so say 'the smallest cable'.

findings.where: Step 9 text, explain paragraphs 5 and 6, practice list
findings.what: 'One maker allows', 'one maker's 2.23 V' and 'For one maker's vented cells' read as source talk, so give them as example values ('Say the float is 2.23 V a cell, with each cell allowed 0.05 V below to 0.10 V above it') and keep the single 'makers ask' line.
'as lesson 4 showed' and 'the gassing voltage from lesson 5' talk about the course, so say 'Kept up, that overcharge helps corrode its positive grid' and 'climbs towards its gassing voltage'.

findings.where: interactive.whatAmILookingAt (shown in the dossier as 'What you're looking at')
findings.what: It holds build notes ('On a phone the three readouts wrap onto a second line', 'Each show screen has under about 90 words', 'Screen by screen. 0 shows...') that read as talk about the course, and only one or two readouts ever show at once, so keep it to what is drawn and the rule.

findings.where: Caption under the panel, and step 2's question, at 360 px
findings.what: '80' and 'Ah' break across lines ('one of 80 / Ah' in the caption, 'the 80 / Ah cell' in the question), so join numbers to units with a non-breaking space; the caption also describes only the tanks while it sits under the parallel and block screens.

Two items the brief promised are missing: the equalise trigger (cells more than about 0.10 V or 10 points of specific gravity apart, and 40 points means a defective cell) and the four-string limit for parallel strings, which sits in the numbers list but never on a screen, so 'read its specific gravity too' has nothing to compare with.

It switches from 'cell' to 'tank' ('every tank gives the same 10 Ah') without saying the cells are drawn as tanks, which a read-through without the picture needs, so say 'Each cell is drawn as a tank'.

findings.where: Step 5 (Driven backwards), live line at 10 hours
findings.what: 'All six are flat now, so the current stops' calls the reversed cell flat, so say 'The big cells are flat now, so the current stops'.
